facts.text: Norris was built in 1933 as a model planned community by the Tennessee Valley Authority to house workers building Norris Dam on the Clinch River.
The town’s layout follows the English garden city movement, with winding roads that hug the terrain and a central green reserved for residents.
Norris Creamery was the first milk‑producing plant in the world powered solely by electricity.
During the 1930s, TVA officials excluded black families from Norris, making it a sundown town, a policy that drew NAACP complaints in 1934, 1935, and 1938.
The Museum of Appalachia, founded by John Rice Irwin, is a popular attraction that showcases regional history and culture in Norris.
The Norris Historical Society, located at 1 Norris Square, preserves the town’s legacy and welcomes visitors during normal business hours.
